Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The Pakistan players make their way out to the middle, followed by Kevin Kasuza and Tarisai Musakanda. Prince Masvaure is not opening as he suffered an injury. Shaheen Afridi will start with the ball.

Zimbabwe's bowling was good in patches. They did not have a great time towards the end of Day 1 but Day 2 was a much-improved performance but they were still on the back foot. They have done a good job to bowl out Pakistan quickly on Day 3 but they still have a long way to go. Blessing Muzarabani was the star of the show with a four-fer while there was no real support from the others. Can they make a fist now with the bat? We will find out in a while.

Pakistan started off well with Abid Ali and Imran Butt doing a very good job with the bat. They stitched a more than 100-run stand and put Pakistan on the ascendancy. Imran Butt scored a fine 91 and then they lost a few wickets but Fawad Alam scored his 4th Test century and put Pakistan well on top. They will be very happy and they hold all the cards at the moment.

Excellent innings from Fawad Alam comes to an end and that brings Pakistan's innings to a close. It has been a superb performance from Pakistan and they are well ahead in this game. They will be very happy with the performance and now they will hope that their bowlers can do the job. Zimbabwe, on the other hand, need to bat really well if they want to make a fist of this game.

We are all set to begin Day 3. The Zimbabwe players are out in the middle. Fawad Alam and Hasan Ali will resume their innings for Pakistan. Blessing Muzarabani will start the proceedings for Zimbabwe on Day 3.

Pitch report - Tino Mawoyo says that there was rain earlier but we are going to have a prompt start. States that the pitch started to misbehave and Zimbabwe will have a tough ask. He is joined by Morne Van Wyk who says that there are footmarks on this pitch and it has been hard going for Zimbabwe. Tells that the batters will look to play a lot straighter. Adds that Pakistan used the depth of the crease well and rotate strike well.

Imran Butt says that they have to keep themselves motivated and need to have energy throughout. Adds that they talk to each other the same way if they played well or not. States that he tries to focus on every ball and he tries to switch on and off every ball. Tells that they have a lot of time left in the Test match.

Donald Tiripano says that on this pitch, they need to execute their plans and they cannot afford to miss. Adds that the ball was reversive and the wicket is abrasive and it is going to be like that for the rest of the game. Adds that they had a good discussion and they executed their plans on Day 2. States that the key is to bowl them out quickly and they need to make sure that they bat for long.

Fawad Alam is on 108 and they would be looking to add as many runs as possible before getting Zimbabwe to bat again. Zimbabwe, on the other hand, would look to clean up the Pakistan's innings quickly and then they will need to bat really well to make a fist of this. Join us in a while.

Right! That's all from Day 2. Pakistan have run away with the show once again. Their lead has crossed 190 and they will return on Day 3 to extend it as much as they can and then run over the opposition again. Let's see how things pan out on Day 3. The action on Day 3, the moving day of the Test match will begin at 0930 local (0730 GMT). Do join us then. For now, it is goodbye from our end. Cheers and take care.

Zimbabwe did not bowl badly. But they failed to take wickets regularly. In the first session, they managed just one. In the second session, Pakistan started getting the runs quicker than they did in the morning session. Tiripano's twin strikes, including the wicket of Babar, gave them a chance of forcing Pakistan on the back foot but they failed to apply the pressure and Alam just ran away with the day with a stupendous century. It was a long day for their bowlers. All the 3 pacers have bowled over 20 overs while Chisoro has bowled 34 overs. So, a hard-fought day for them.

The day started with the Zimbabwe bowlers bowling really tight lines and lengths in the first hour of the session. Pakistan lost Abid in the first session but they managed to up the scoring rate a touch with Azhar playing a few shots. However, Azhar departed at the start of the second session and Babar, the skipper, bagged a golden duck, his first in Tests. Imran Butt, the Pakistani opener, got to his half ton and was looking set for his 100 but he played a loose shot to throw his wicket away. However, Alam wasn't going to throw his wicket away. He along with Rizwan added 107 and extended the Pakistani lead. Alam has kept his conversion rate to 100% as he raked up his ton. Rizwan fell and Faheem fell soon but Fawad has made sure that he will return on Day 3 to continue from where he has stopped here.

Another amazing day of the Test for Pakistan. A superb knock from Fawad Alam and he is not done yet. Pakistan have extended their lead to 198 in this session and are clearly on the driving seat. A tough session for Zimbabwe. They did get wickets but they have given away runs at nearly 3 runs per over. Big test ahead for them.

The Zimbabwe bowlers tried hard in this session. They got the rewards too as they got 3 wickets. However, with the Pakistani batters approaching the aggressive route in this one, they have given away runs at over 3 per over. So, when they return for the final session on Day 2, they will look to break this stand quickly and force a collapse if they are to keep the lead small. Pakistan would aim otherwise. Join us for the final session to find out how things pan out.

Azhar was the first one to depart as he was removed by Tiripano. Tiripano then got the better of Babar as he sent him packing on the very first ball, with a well-set plan from the skipper. Butt continued but fell into the 90s. However, it is Fawad who has got the scoreboard moving for them. He has reached his half-century and would look to convert this one into a ton too. He has Rizwan for the company and the duo will look to do the same in the next session.

Another very good session of Test match cricket. In this session, Zimbabwe struck. They struck twice quickly. However, Fawad walked in and took the bowlers on. He took a bit of an aggressive approach and helped Pakistan take the lead. Pakistan's lead has already grown to 85 and their aim would be to just keep batting. Zimbabwe have done well to get 3 wickets this session but they need to get more in the final one to make sure they do not give away a big, big lead.

We are back for the second session. The Zimbabwe players have made their way out in the middle following the two umpires. Imran Butt and Azhar Ali will resume their innings. Tendai Chisoro will start the proceedings for Zimbabwe in this session.
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

Credit to Zimbabwe for not giving free runs. All of their bowlers bowled really tight lines and lengths. However, they need wickets to get a grip on the game. Pakistan is just 14 behind from their first innings score and if they do not get quick wickets, the visitors will take a big lead by the end of Day 2. Join us for the afternoon session in a short while.

In the first hour, the Pakistani batters couldn't score freely. They failed to hit a single boundary and could muster only 13 runs before the Drinks break. Abid fell soon after the Drinks break. Azhar Ali walked in, hit a few boundaries and has added 47 with Imran so far. Butt got to his half ton and since then he too has done well to keep the scoreboard ticking. The duo will look to return and grow their stand.

A very engrossing session of play! Zimbabwe have done well with the ball as they have kept things tight in this session. However, Pakistan have scored a bit freely in the second hour, it is still very good bowling from Zimbabwe. Just 59 runs scored in 32 overs. The visitors will not be too disappointed with their performance as they have lost just one wicket.

It is time for the action. The Zimbabwe players are out in the middle. The two Pakistani openers, Abid Ali and Imran Butt will resume for Pakistan. Blessing Muzarabani will start with the ball for his side. All set. Here we go...

Pitch report - Tino Mawoyo is in with the pitch report for Day 2. Mawoyo says the weather is superb. Adds that the ball was moving early on in the first day. Adds that the ball was spinning as well. Tells that the batting will be once again good and it will remain that way for the next 2 days too.

Younis Khan, the Pakistan batting coach, is up for a chat. He says that it was a good bowling performance from them after losing the toss. Hopes that they bat long and bat once. Feels the batters need to play according to the situation and keep taking the singles which are always key.

Roy Kaia is in for a chat before the action begins. Roy says that the wicket looks like a good batting track and it was nice to bat out there. Adds that as a debutant, there will always be pressure at the start but feels he overcame that. Says that as a batter they need to spend time in the crease and feels they played a few poor shots.

How will Day 2 pan out? Will we see the Pakistani batting piling up the runs? They will be aiming to bat long and bat once. Can Zimbabwe produce something magical with the ball on Day 2? They would look to strike early and turn things around. Let's see how things pan out on Day 2. Action to begin in a short while.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the first Test match between Pakistan and Zimbabwe. Pakistan took the honors on Day 1 as they rolled over the hosts for a low score and have already reduced the deficit with Abid Ali getting to his half ton and his opening partner closing in towards his half century.

In reply, the Pakistan openers have already added 100 between them and they have scored quite freely. More of the same is what Pakistan would want and they would hope to bat Zimbabwe out of the game.

End of a superb day for Pakistan! They have dominated it completely. After being asked to field, their pacers Shaheen Afridi and Hasan Ali ran riot! Both finished with 4 each. Roy was the only batter for Zimbabwe who showed some fight.
